title: Language-model credence updates moved outside the starting opinion range
summary: In a controlled study of eight instruction-tuned language models, 22% to 68% of updates fell outside the interval between the two stated starting credences. Depending on model, 4% to 38% did so opposite the drift measured without peer input. Small model populations also sometimes spread farther apart under schedules that never widened opinions in a classical averaging comparison.
ai_technology: Qwen2.5; Gemma; Llama 3.1; Mistral 7B; token-probability credence readout

evidence.tested: Across 73,080 operator measurements, 22.3%–68.3% of model updates left the initial opinion interval, and 3.7%–38.0% did so opposite the no-peer drift. Small model populations widened their opinion range in 5.9%–25.6% of rounds, versus zero for a DeGroot averaging comparison using the same schedules.
evidence.unknown: The readout concerns single-claim scores in a fixed prompt design, not general belief or human behavior. The study used models no larger than 9 billion parameters, some with quantization. The 10,000-agent analysis was a simulation of fitted functions.
evidence.ai_role: Eight instruction-tuned Qwen, Gemma, Llama and Mistral models responded to controlled scalar credence exchanges. Output token probabilities gave observable estimates of the updated credence, with matched no-peer controls.
